name: HateCheck
contains: ACL 2021 functional test suite for hate speech detection: test cases with labels, functionality annotations and template placeholder values.
use: Run each case through the filter and score per functionality, especially non-hateful contrasts (counter-speech, reclaimed slurs, negation) as hard negatives.

name: XSTest
contains: NAACL 2024 test suite of safe prompts that superficially resemble unsafe ones (plus unsafe contrasts) for exaggerated-safety evaluation, with eval code and model completions.
use: Feed the safe prompts as must-not-block hard negatives and the unsafe contrasts as must-flag; measure over-refusal rate.
note: README states prompts are CC-BY-4.0; model completions are under the original model providers' licences. Mainly over-refusal, only loosely prompt_injection.

name: CheckList
contains: Code/framework for behavioural testing of NLP models (templates, perturbations, MFT/INV/DIR tests) from the ACL 2020 paper.
use: Generate invariance/perturbation variants (typos, negation, name swaps) of filter test rows to check the verdict is stable.
note: Repo page shows 'MIT license'. Tool, not a dataset.

name: Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification (Wikipedia talk comments)
licence: CC0-1.0 (labels); comment text CC BY-SA 3.0 per Hugging Face loader (TFDS says CC0) - conflicting
contains: Wikipedia talk-page comments labelled toxic / severe_toxic / obscene / threat / insult / identity_hate.
use: Use the insult/obscene/threat-labelled rows as must-flag and clean rows as must-pass; report per-label recall and false-positive rate.
note: Kaggle page returned only a title, no licence (likely JS/login wall). HF loader _LICENSE: dataset CC0, comment text 'governed by Wikipedia's CC-SA-3.0'. TFDS catalog (tensorflow.org/datasets/catalog/wikipedia_toxicity_subtypes) says CC0 'as is the underlying comment text'. Sources conflict; treat text as CC BY-SA 3.0 to be safe.

name: Civil Comments
contains: About 2M English public comments from the Civil Comments platform (2015-2017) with fractional toxicity scores for 7 attributes (toxicity, severe_toxicity, obscene, threat, insult, identity_attack, sexual_explicit).
use: Threshold the insult/obscene scores (e.g. >=0.5 flag, <0.1 clean) to build must-flag and must-pass sets; identity mentions in clean rows give bias hard negatives.
note: Card states 'This dataset is released under CC0 1.0', tag cc0-1.0.

name: OLID / OffensEval 2019
contains: About 14,100 English tweets with hierarchical labels: offensive or not, targeted or not, target type (individual/group/other).
use: Use OFF/TIN rows as insult must-flag and NOT rows as must-pass; TIN+GRP rows overlap hate speech.
note: HF card License field reads '[More Information Needed]'. Official sites.google.com/site/offensevalsharedtask/olid redirects to a Google sign-in. Web search found no licence for the dataset itself. Tweet text is also subject to X/Twitter terms.

name: UCI SMS Spam Collection
contains: 5,574 English SMS messages, each labelled spam or ham (legitimate).
use: Spam rows are must-flag and ham rows must-pass.
note: UCI page states 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license'.

name: deepset prompt-injections
contains: 662 labelled prompts (546 train / 116 test), injection vs benign, in English and German.
use: Label-1 rows must flag as injection and label-0 rows must pass; the German rows test whether the filter is English-only.
note: Card metadata licence: apache-2.0. Languages are inferred from the examples; the card does not state them.

name: Lakera gandalf_ignore_instructions
contains: About 1,000 real English 'ignore previous instructions'-style injection prompts from the Gandalf game (777/111/112 split).
use: Positives only: every row should be flagged as injection. Pair it with a benign set (e.g. deepset label-0) for the false-positive rate.
note: Card states 'distributed under the MIT License'; metadata mit.

name: CLINC150 (oos-eval)
contains: English intent-classification data: 150 in-scope intents (22,500 queries) plus 1,200 out-of-scope queries.
use: Treat a chosen subset of in-scope intents as 'on topic' and the oos queries (and the other intents) as off-topic must-flag; measure topic-gate precision and recall.
note: The repo page does not name the licence; the LICENSE file was fetched and is 'Attribution 3.0 Unported' (CC BY 3.0).

name: ai4privacy pii-masking-200k
licence: custom: Ai4Privacy free licence (individuals, non-profits, for-profits with up to 3 staff); corporate licence otherwise; no redistribution of copies or derivatives
contains: About 209k synthetic examples (13.6M tokens, 649k PII tokens) in English, French, German and Italian, with source text, masked target, PII spans and BIO tags.
use: Run the source_text through the PII filter and score span-level recall against the labels; the masked target_text gives must-pass rows.
note: Card YAML has no licence field; the repo LICENSE file sets out custom Free and Corporate licence tiers. Not an open licence: check the staff-size limit and keep it local, never redistributed.

name: Microsoft Presidio (+ presidio-research)
contains: Python SDK for PII detection and de-identification (analyzer, anonymizer, CLI, image redactor, structured). The companion presidio-research repo has a template-based fake-PII sentence generator and evaluation tooling.
use: Use the presidio-research generator to make labelled synthetic PII sentences locally, and use the analyzer as a baseline to compare the filter against.
note: Both repos show 'MIT license' (presidio-research also checked: https://github.com/microsoft/presidio-research). This is a tool, not a dataset.

name: OpenAI moderation-api-release
contains: 1,680 labelled samples across 8 categories (sexual, hate, violence, harassment, self-harm, sexual/minors, hate/threatening, violence/graphic).
use: Pointer only: per-category must-flag and must-pass evaluation rows. Do NOT pull the sexual/minors rows into the local corpus; use the label only.
note: Repo page shows 'MIT license'. Small set, so per-category counts are low.

name: Internet Watch Foundation (IWF)
contains: UK charity for reporting and removing online CSAM. Its technology page lists an Image Hash List, IntelliGrade, Report Remove, IWF Crawler, reThink Chatbot and Image Intercept, offered through membership.
use: Do not collect child-safety test data. Route detection to IWF services (hash list via membership) and report through IWF; test the filter only with clean, non-abusive proxy rows.
note: Home page and technology page both loaded. No URL list or keyword list is shown on the pages fetched; membership has entry criteria (https://www.iwf.org.uk/become-a-member/join-us).

name: Thorn Safer
contains: Thorn's commercial trust-and-safety product for CSAM and child sexual exploitation detection (perceptual hashing and ML classifiers).
use: Treat as a vendor detection service, not a source of test data; never build a local CSAM corpus.
note: Page loaded. It is a commercial product with no dataset licence, and the page does not explicitly mention text classifiers.

name: Samaritans: industry guidelines for managing self-harm and suicide content
contains: Samaritans' best-practice principles and information sheets for user-generated-content platforms on handling self-harm and suicide content. The parent page also links 'guidance for online services'.
use: Derive the expected-behaviour spec (safe-messaging, signposting, no method detail) for self-harm test rows; it is not a dataset.
note: The given URL (.../internet-suicide/) also resolves and is the hub; this sub-page is the specific industry guidance. No reuse licence stated; the site footer links /legal/.
